own_solution.law: Joule heating in an ohmic resistor: P = V^2 / R
assumptions: 12.0 V is the voltage across the resistor itself
resistance is 8.0 ohm at operating conditions

notes: P = (12.0 V)^2 / 8.0 ohm = 144/8 = 18 W in all four renderings. The ambient pressure (18, 36, 72, 144 kPa) has no physical path to the dissipated power when V and R are given directly (structurally disconnected, D). All four renderings differ only in the pressure value, so the answer is invariant at 18 W. The pressure sentence is a little artificial in a bench electronics context, and 18 kPa is an unusually low ambient pressure for a bench (roughly 12 km altitude equivalent), but it does not affect the answer.
